findings.description: The new null/zero return from to_bytes_expand is not checked by ECDSA sign for r_bytes or s_bytes. The unchanged caller computes result_size from the returned lengths, allocates result, copies and proceeds toward ArrayBuffer return. A failed r or s allocation has no explicit OOM return before those operations.
findings.sourceCounterexample: Let r conversion return {nullptr,0} and s conversion return an owned32-byte result, then let result allocation succeed. The caller proceeds with result_size32 and a null source in the zero-length r memcpy; the symmetric s case has the same propagation gap. This is static control-flow reasoning, not an observed fault or successful malformed signature.
findings.consequence: The proposed shared-helper failure return is not integrated through every caller. A pending JS allocation error does not replace an explicit caller control-flow guard.
findings.scope: All fifteen import/export sites have pointer checks; only these two ECDSA sign sites are unchecked. Other BIGNUM and EC point ownership findings remain source-qualified.
findings.requiredCorrection: In a new immutable successor, check each r/s returned owner and report the existing JS_ReportOutOfMemory plus return nullptr before result-size/result-allocation/copy/ArrayBuffer creation on failure. Preserve successful behavior and original proposal/erratum.

The null check now precedes helper-local padding/pointer arithmetic/BN export, but M1 prevents treating it as complete shared-helper error propagation.
